warnings.label: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
warnings.description: Tidal Thames riverside from Putney Bridge to Teddington Weir
warnings.county: Greater London, Hammersmith and Fulham, Hounslow, Richmond upon Thames, Wandsworth
warnings.eaArea: Kent, South London and East Sussex
warnings.message:
High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 04:30 AM to 06:30 AM on Saturday 15 August. 
The forecast high tide at Richmond is 4.60 mAOD at 05:30 AM on Saturday 15th August.

Locations most affected will be Putney Embankment (SW15), Chiswick Mall and Strand on the Green (W4), Thames Bank at Mortlake (SW14), Ranelagh Drive (TW1), Friars Lane and Water Lane (TW9), Riverside and The Embankment at Twickenham, and the Towpath below Teddington Lock. Flooding of properties is not expected.

Astronomical tide levels are rising/falling. The river flow at Teddington Weir is 3 cubic metres per second and is steady. We anticipate the flows to remain steady for the next few days. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 15 August 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Hunstanton coast in Norfolk
warnings.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from 06.45am to 10.45am on Saturday 15 August. 
Areas most at risk are around Hunstanton seafront.  Flood gates in the area will be closed by the Local Authority which will make access difficult. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at King's Lynn of 4.54mAODN at 08:45am on 15 August 2026, Wind Force 5, North Westerly. The high tide tomorrow evening is not expected to be as high. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 11:00AM on 15 August 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Somerset coast at Porlock Weir
warnings.message:
The current sequence of high Spring tides, peaks this evening and may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible around 21:00 on Friday 14th August. 
Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. 
The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Hinkley of 6.49 mAODN at 21:00 on 14/08/26, which is 1.02m above tide tables, with Westerly force 5 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.)
After the high tide at 21:00 on 14/8/26, the weather is forecast to improve and no further flooding is expected.
We are closely monitoring the situation. 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. 
This message will be updated by 12:00AM on 15 August 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: Coast at North Morecambe Bay
warnings.message:
High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible from from 00:45 to 02:15 on 15/08/2026. 
Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths along the coast at North Morecambe Bay from Roosebeck to Carnforth including low lying areas around Ulverston, Greenodd, Haverthwaite, Flookburgh, Grange-over-Sands, Levens, Milnthorpe, Sandside, Arnside and Silverdale.
We are nearing the end of a period of high spring tides and are not expecting any further tides to reach Flood Alert Level in this cycle. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water  
This message will be updated by 10:00AM on 15 August 2026 or as the situation changes.

warnings.label: The tidal Deben estuary
warnings.message:
High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 1.15 am and 3.15 am tomorrow morning, Saturday 15th August. 
Tide levels will be high around the boat yard in Felixstowe Ferry hamlet at the end of Ferry Road, and along riverside areas in Woodbridge and Waldringfield, as well as in surrounding marshland. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Harwich of 2.54mAODN at 2.15am, on Saturday 15th August, which is 0.34m above tide tables, Wind Force 3, North Easterly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 9:00AM on 15 August 2026 or as the situation changes.
